name: LangGraph / LangChain
summary: LangChain is the higher-level agent framework and integrations layer; LangGraph is its lower-level orchestration runtime for long-running, stateful agents. LangGraph documents persistence, durable execution, streaming and human-in-the-loop. It can be used without LangChain. Both are current projects.
languages: Python documented; JavaScript/TypeScript parity needs verification.
deployment: Run application workers locally or self-hosted; LangSmith deployment is a separate managed option.
strengths: Choice of lower-level runtime or higher-level integrations
limitations: Low-level LangGraph deliberately does not abstract prompt or agent architecture. Durable execution still requires deterministic/replay-safe design and idempotent side effects; exact operational guarantees depend on the checkpointer and deployment choice.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT for the open-source repositories; LangSmith is a separate commercial platform.
maturity: Active documentation and repositories reviewed. Selected package version and deployment recovery not tested here.

name: Microsoft Agent Framework
summary: Current Microsoft framework for agents, an opinionated harness, graph/functional workflows and provider/hosting integrations. Microsoft’s official resource page identifies a production-ready 1.0 release for .NET and Python in April 2026 and provides migration paths from AutoGen and Semantic Kernel orchestration.
languages: .NET/C# and Python; current docs also expose Go views. Verify feature parity.
deployment: Self-hosted applications or supported managed hosting integrations, including Functions; check chosen hosting contract.
strengths: Documented migration paths from Microsoft predecessors
limitations: Provider and tool features vary. Microsoft explicitly advises simpler direct model calls when orchestration is not needed. Migration suitability from mature AutoGen/Semantic Kernel systems requires feature-by-feature validation.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT for the SDK repository. Managed Microsoft services and third-party providers have separate terms.
maturity: Microsoft documents a 1.0 release and migration paths. This catalogue has not run cross-language or recovery tests.

name: CrewAI
summary: Maintained Python framework with two principal abstractions: role-based collaborating “Crews” and event-driven “Flows” that can include deterministic code, model calls and crews. CrewAI AMP is a separate managed deployment/monitoring product.
languages: Python framework.
deployment: Embed locally or self-host; CrewAI AMP is a separate managed deployment product.
strengths: Explicit event-driven flows alongside autonomous crews
limitations: Crews add autonomy and coordination overhead; Flows are the more explicit control path. Exact persistence, replay and failure guarantees of a chosen deployment were not established by the overview and need a failure POC. Optional sharing can collect crew/task inputs and outputs when enabled.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT for the open-source framework; AMP terms are separate.
maturity: Active framework and managed product documentation reviewed; exact replay and persistence guarantees remain POC requirements.

name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
summary: Current Google-led, model- and deployment-agnostic agent development kit covering agents, tools, sessions/memory, evaluation and multi-agent composition. It integrates closely with Gemini and Google Cloud without requiring them.
languages: Python, Java, Go, JavaScript and Kotlin documentation; verify SDK-specific features.
deployment: Local applications, Cloud Run, GKE and managed Agent Engine/Runtime paths are documented.
strengths: Multiple local and managed deployment paths
limitations: Managed Google deployment capabilities and SDK features are not necessarily portable across runtimes or languages. Confirm service region, identity, session persistence and model/tool support for the target environment.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Apache-2.0 for Google’s ADK repositories.
maturity: Maintained Google-led ecosystem; SDK parity and target-region support must be verified.

name: PydanticAI
summary: Current Python SDK centered on typed agent inputs, dependencies, tools and structured outputs, with graph, evaluation, observability, harness and realtime capabilities.
languages: Python SDK.
deployment: Run in an application; durable integrations use separate runtimes such as Temporal or DBOS.
limitations: Typing/schema validation does not establish semantic correctness. Durable integrations replay work and therefore still demand deterministic workflow code and idempotent side effects; retry defaults vary by engine (the docs flag unbounded Temporal activity attempts unless configured).
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT for the repository.
maturity: Active typed-agent SDK. Schema validation does not establish business correctness; runtime durability needs separate evidence.

name: AutoGen
summary: Microsoft Research framework with AgentChat (high-level conversational agents), Core (event-driven actor/runtime layer), extensions and Studio. AutoGen 0.4 was a breaking rewrite of 0.2. Microsoft now directs new production orchestration evaluation toward Microsoft Agent Framework, while AutoGen remains relevant existing/research technology.
languages: Python AgentChat; other Core worker language support requires verification.
deployment: Embedded local or distributed Core runtime depending on the selected API.
limitations: 0.2 and 0.4 APIs differ materially, and the old migration guide listed feature gaps. State save/load is not by itself crash-safe durable execution. Establish maintenance/migration strategy before new adoption.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT. The `pyautogen` package after 0.2.34 is not controlled by Microsoft; use official package names/repository.
maturity: Existing/research technology with Microsoft Agent Framework migration guidance. Decide maintenance strategy before new adoption.

name: Semantic Kernel
summary: Maintained Microsoft SDK for model integration, plugins/functions, prompt templates, memory/connectors and agent-related application features. Microsoft Agent Framework is now the primary Microsoft lead for new multi-agent orchestration; Semantic Kernel remains relevant where its kernel/plugin abstractions or existing investments fit.
languages: C#/.NET, Python and Java.
deployment: Embed the SDK in your application; hosting and connected services are separate choices.
strengths: Useful fit for existing .NET and other SDK investments
limitations: Do not conflate Semantic Kernel’s agent APIs with the newer Microsoft Agent Framework. Some agent features historically used provider APIs with their own lifecycle/deprecation constraints; verify each chosen agent type and migration path.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT.
maturity: Maintained SDK with existing plugin investments; inspect migration guidance for new agent orchestration.

name: LlamaIndex
summary: Maintained data-centric framework for ingestion, indexing, retrieval/RAG, agents and event-driven workflows. Its older Query Pipeline is feature-frozen/deprecated in favor of Workflows.
languages: Python; verify TypeScript feature parity.
deployment: Application-managed RAG/workflows; LlamaCloud and related deployment products have separate boundaries.
limitations: The broad connector ecosystem varies in maintenance and operational behavior. Persistence and durable/replay behavior depend on selected workflow/runtime integrations; validate update/delete propagation and access filtering for RAG workloads.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT for the core repository.
maturity: Active data framework; legacy Query Pipeline is deprecated. Select the current workflow API explicitly.

name: Haystack
summary: Maintained Python framework for component-based LLM, retrieval and agentic pipelines. Directed multigraph pipelines support branches, loops and concurrent flows; agents can be built from pipeline components.
languages: Python.
deployment: Self-host application pipelines, including Docker; managed/enterprise offerings are separate.
limitations: Pipeline durability, cross-process checkpoints and exactly-once effects are not established by the core pipeline overview. Integration packages have independent compatibility and should be pinned/tested.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Apache-2.0 for Haystack.
maturity: Active component framework. Core pipeline overview does not establish crash-safe replay or external exactly-once effects.

name: Agno
summary: Current Python stack spanning an agent/team/workflow SDK, AgentOS runtime and a control-plane UI. It emphasizes self-hosted services, sessions, memory, knowledge, guardrails, human review and observability.
languages: Python SDK; other language SDKs unverified.
deployment: Self-host AgentOS/application services and their databases; control-plane terms need separate review.
strengths: Separately described runtime and control-plane layers
limitations: Framework, runtime and control plane are distinct layers. Agno sends limited model-usage telemetry by default according to its repository; it can be disabled. Validate stateless runtime/database responsibilities and durable failure behavior.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Apache-2.0 for the core SDK. Control-plane/cloud licensing and feature boundaries require separate verification.
maturity: Active framework/runtime/control-plane ecosystem. Telemetry configuration and recovery behavior require deployment review.

name: Strands Agents
summary: Current open agent harness SDK originating from Amazon production systems, with tools, hooks, MCP, structured output, sessions and multi-agent patterns.
languages: Python and TypeScript; verify feature parity.
deployment: Local/container applications or supported AWS and Kubernetes deployment paths; non-AWS providers are supported.
limitations: AWS integrations are optional but have separate service semantics and costs. Feature parity across Python/TypeScript and durable guarantees for each deployment path require verification; the harness alone does not make external effects exactly-once.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Apache-2.0 across official projects.
maturity: Active SDK; TypeScript repository moved to a monorepo. Deployment-specific durability remains untested here.

name: Temporal
summary: Mature durable-execution platform for application workflows and activities; it is not agent-specific. A self-hosted server and Temporal Cloud are available.
languages: Go, Java, PHP, Python, TypeScript and .NET SDKs documented.
deployment: Application workers connect to self-hosted Temporal Service or commercial Temporal Cloud.
limitations: Workflow code must remain deterministic under replay and version changes. Activities can execute more than once after ambiguous failures, so idempotency remains an application duty. Operating the self-hosted service adds database, upgrades and observability work.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: MIT for the open-source server and SDKs; Temporal Cloud has commercial terms.
maturity: Established durable-execution platform. Deterministic replay, versioning and activity idempotency remain application duties.

name: Azure Durable Functions
summary: Azure Functions extension built on Durable Task for stateful serverless orchestrations, activities and entities. It manages checkpoints, retries and recovery; standalone self-hosted Durable Task SDKs are now another hosting model.
languages: C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Java and PowerShell in Functions; verify self-hosted SDK parity.
deployment: Azure Functions durable extension or supported Durable Task hosting; storage/provider constraints vary.
limitations: Orchestrators replay and must obey deterministic-code restrictions. Storage provider, plan limits, execution duration, history growth and versioning need workload-specific checks. External activities are not guaranteed exactly once.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Open-source Durable Functions/Task SDK repositories use MIT; Azure hosting and Durable Task Scheduler are paid services with separate terms.
maturity: Established Functions capability. Test selected storage provider, orchestration constraints and version migration.

name: Dapr Workflow
summary: Current Dapr building block for long-running, fault-tolerant application workflows, integrated with Dapr service invocation, pub/sub, state and bindings. Runtime scheduling occurs in the Dapr sidecar.
languages: Python, JavaScript, .NET, Java and Go workflow SDKs documented.
deployment: Applications run with Dapr sidecars and a compatible state store, often on Kubernetes.
strengths: Workflow building block beside other Dapr capabilities
limitations: Only compatible state stores may be used. Workflow functions must be deterministic and same-thread constraints apply. Default dispatch payload ceiling is 4 MiB; near-limit histories can stall. Cosmos DB and DynamoDB have documented complexity limitations.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Apache-2.0 for Dapr.
maturity: Active Dapr building block. State-store and payload limitations must be checked against the pinned runtime.

name: n8n
summary: Maintained visual/low-code workflow automation product with a large integration catalog, code nodes and AI/agent nodes. It is a general automation platform, not primarily a durable code-first agent runtime.
languages: Node.js application; visual workflows with feature-specific JavaScript/Python code support.
deployment: n8n Cloud or self-hosted Docker/npm; queue mode adds database/Redis operations.
limitations: Node behavior, credential handling, execution retention and retry semantics vary. Community nodes expand supply-chain risk. Confirm queue-mode topology, binary-data storage, licensing and idempotency before production writes.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Source-available Sustainable Use License for most code, not OSI open source; enterprise files/features have a proprietary license. Internal business use is generally permitted, while white-label/hosting-for-fee and some customer-credential product uses require agreement.
maturity: Maintained product under source-available licensing; not an OSI-open-source classification. Verify intended commercial use.

name: Hindsight
summary: Active Vectorize project providing long-term agent memory with retain, recall and reflect operations and structured factual, experiential and belief-like memory. It complements an agent/runtime rather than replacing orchestration.
languages: Server API with SDK/integration clients; exact current client-language matrix unverified.
deployment: Server-oriented memory service with self-hosting documentation; verify storage and edition requirements.
strengths: Can complement rather than replace a task runtime
limitations: Published benchmark claims are not universal production evidence. Memory can be stale, inferred or poisoned; applications still need tenant isolation, provenance, deletion propagation and authorization outside conversational memory.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: The repository currently identifies an open-source project, but the exact license text/edition boundaries were not verified from a reviewed primary license page; check before adoption.
maturity: Emerging memory layer; exact license and production guarantees were not established by reviewed pages.

name: Flue
summary: Emerging TypeScript agent framework/harness built around synchronous agent functions plus hooks for models, tools, sandboxes, skills, subagents and persisted state. It can run standalone or integrate with workflow systems.
languages: TypeScript/JavaScript.
deployment: Local, CI or backend execution; documented Cloudflare-oriented and workflow integrations.
strengths: Hooks for tools and workflow integrations
limitations: Newer ecosystem with less independently established maturity. Agent definition functions must be synchronous; async work moves to tools/hooks/resources. Verify database adapter durability, migrations, sandbox isolation and non-Cloudflare production behavior.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Marketed as open, but the exact repository license and commercial-service boundaries were unverified from the reviewed pages.
maturity: Emerging ecosystem. Exact license, persistence adapters and non-Cloudflare production behavior require verification.

name: Paperclip
summary: Emerging control plane for organizing external coding/agent runtimes as “AI employees”: companies, org structure, assignments/issues, approvals, budgets, costs and audit records. It is a management/orchestration layer above Claude, Codex, Gemini or custom adapters, not a model SDK.
languages: External runtime adapters; exact product implementation requirements unverified.
deployment: Install locally, in Docker or on a server; workers depend on configured external runtimes.
limitations: Heartbeat execution is burst-based, not a continuously running worker. Reliability depends on adapter session persistence and agent cooperation with task APIs. Human organizational metaphors do not supply transactionality, safe delegation or semantic correctness.
Exact package version and all required capability tests must be recorded in your proof of concept; not pinned by this catalogue.
license: Presented as open source, but the exact license and edition boundaries were unverified from a reviewed primary license page.
maturity: Emerging agent management/control plane. Heartbeat-based work is not itself a durable execution guarantee.

name: Thin custom loop + provider SDK
summary: A small application-owned loop around a model API and a restricted set of tools.
languages: Choose a language supported by the selected SDK or HTTP API.
deployment: Your existing application or worker environment.
strengths: No agent framework required for a small loop
limitations: You implement state, policy, budgets, retries and verification.
Provider capabilities and commercial terms need current verification.
license: Your code and selected dependency licenses; provider terms separate.
maturity: Architecture baseline, not a product release or vendor support claim.

name: Conventional rules and integration
summary: Deterministic rules, scheduled jobs, APIs and queues without model decisions.
languages: Use the team’s existing supported stack.
deployment: Existing service, scheduler or queue worker.
strengths: Avoids model inference cost and variability
limitations: Ambiguous unstructured interpretation may require humans or a separate model step.
External effects still require authorization and recovery.
license: Depends on selected components.
maturity: Established engineering pattern; fitness depends on process stability and exceptions.
